hevc.windowsBody: Your Windows is missing the HEVC codec, so HEVC files use slow software decode. Installing Microsoft's HEVC Video Extension lets your GPU decode them — fixes 4K HEVC. Note: 8K HEVC is beyond most GPUs even with the codec.
hevc.linuxBody:
Your Linux Chromium is using software HEVC decode, which stutters on 4K+ files. To enable hardware decode, install your distro's VA-API drivers and restart FunSync:
# Ubuntu / Debian (Intel iGPU)
sudo apt install intel-media-va-driver mesa-va-drivers

# Ubuntu / Debian (AMD GPU)
sudo apt install mesa-va-drivers

# Ubuntu / Debian (NVIDIA, recent drivers)
sudo apt install nvidia-vaapi-driver

# Fedora
sudo dnf install libva-utils mesa-va-drivers-freeworld

# Arch
sudo pacman -S libva-utils intel-media-driver libva-mesa-driver
Note: 8K HEVC is beyond most GPUs even with hardware decode.
hevc.macosBody: Your macOS Chromium can't use VideoToolbox HEVC — this usually means you're on macOS 10.12 or older (HEVC requires 10.13+). Update macOS to enable hardware HEVC decode. Note: even on supported macOS, 8K HEVC needs an Apple Silicon Mac (M1/M2/M3) — older Intel Macs top out around 4K HEVC.
hevc.genericBody: HEVC files in your library will use slow software decode on this platform and may stutter, especially at 4K and above.

playback.gapHint: Gaps shorter than the threshold are ignored. Press G to skip manually.
playback.upNextHint: Shows the next item in the current library / playlist / category at the end of the video, with an autoplay countdown. Hover the card to pause the countdown; click × or press Esc to dismiss.
playback.multiHint: When set to Multi-axis, FunSync auto-assigns multi-axis playback to videos with detected companion files (twist, surge, etc.). Already-set videos keep their current selection. Switching back to Single will not revert auto-assignments — use Change funscript on individual videos to undo.
playback.smoothingHint: Interpolation affects Buttplug.io and T-Code devices. Step sends instant jumps with no smoothing — best for scripts that use rapid low-distance motion for vibration. Handy uses its own interpolation and ignores this.
playback.rangeExtenderHint: When a script's stroke positions stay in a narrow range (e.g. 30–70), stretch them so they use the device's full range. Applies to all devices on next video load.
playback.rangeExtenderResetAria: Reset Stretch limited-range scripts to default
playback.orgasmScriptHint: Hold X during playback to swap your device(s) onto this short looping script, then release to snap back. Works with Handy, Buttplug and T-Code.
playback.orgasmModeHint: Hold to ride: hold X to play the looping script, release to return to the main script. Press to finish: tap X to start it looping, tap again to stop the device — it won't return to the main script.
playback.randomVariantHint: When a video has multiple script variations, pick one at random each time it plays. Overrides pinned default variations while on.
playback.bpHint: Per-stroke sends one command per action and lets the device's firmware interpolate — matches how the Handy's WiFi API (HSSP) feels. Lookahead compensates for BLE round-trip; min stroke stretches too-short strokes up so BLE can honor them. For Handy via connection code (HSSP), these have no effect.
playback.inlineVizOpacityHint: How solid the script timeline and heatmap strip look over the video. Turn them on from the player's ⋮ menu.
playback.rememberSpeedHint: Keep the current speed when you load another video. Off by default, so each video starts at 1x.
playback.fillerPreviewAria: Preview of the filler stroke pattern
playback.fillerHint: Plays gentle strokes during long blank stretches of script instead of leaving the device still. Ignored when Gap Skip is set to automatic.

appearance.folderPreviewsHint: Show a mosaic of the videos inside on folder tiles. Turn off to use a plain folder icon instead.
appearance.miniPlayerHint: When you go back to the library while a video is playing, it shrinks into a corner mini-player and keeps playing (and keeps driving your device) instead of stopping.
appearance.hwDecodeHint: On by default. If videos won't play — a black screen or decode error, common on NVIDIA + Linux — turn this off to use software decoding. Takes effect after restarting the app.
appearance.hwDecodeRestart: Restart FunSync to apply the video decoding change.
appearance.cardHeatmapHint: Show a stroke-speed heatmap under each thumbnail. Uses the video's main script. Off by default because it reads a script per card.
appearance.resumeProgressHint: Show how far through each video you got, as a bar on playlist cards and rows. Playlist playback only — the main library is left unmarked.

vrModal.title: VR
vrModal.experimentalText: VR streaming and device sync are still being tuned. Expect rough edges around reconnection, sync timing, and player-specific quirks.
vrModal.streamingIntro: Set up HereSphere to browse and stream FunSync's library directly. No file transfers — works on Quest standalone or PCVR.
vrModal.hsUrlHint: Type this into the URL bar at the top of HereSphere's home screen on your Quest.
vrModal.setupFirstTimeStep2: Type the URL above into HereSphere's URL bar (at the top of the home screen) and press Enter.
vrModal.setupFirstTimeStep3: Your FunSync library appears — pick a video to play.
vrModal.setupFirstTimeStep4: Optional: bookmark or favourite the page in HereSphere so you don't have to retype next time.
vrModal.setupSyncStep2: Enable the timestamp server — required for FunSync to drive non-Handy devices.
vrModal.setupSyncStep3: Check that the IP field shows your Quest's current IP. If it's blank or stale (e.g. your Quest got a new IP since you set this up), press the auto-find button next to the IP field — HereSphere fills it in for you. Port should be 23554.
vrModal.setupSyncStep4: FunSync auto-detects your Quest and connects when you open a video in HereSphere.
vrModal.setupTrUrlBar: URL bar not visible? It's at the top of HereSphere's home screen — tap the address area to bring up the keyboard.
vrModal.setupTrNoVideos: No videos showing? Make sure FunSync is open with at least one source added.
vrModal.setupTrUnreachable: FunSync shows "VR companion can't reach HereSphere's timestamp server", or only the Handy moves while other devices stay silent? HereSphere isn't accepting connections on the address FunSync is reaching for. Two common fixes, in order:
vrModal.setupTrUnreachableStep1: Press the auto-find button next to the IP field in HereSphere's Timestamp Server settings — captures your Quest's current local IP. Useful when the IP has changed since setup (DHCP lease renewed, new router, etc.).
vrModal.setupTrUnreachableStep2: Toggle the timestamp server off and back on — clears any stuck state. HereSphere has had bugs in older versions where the listener didn't re-initialise after switching profiles; toggling fixes that.
vrModal.setupTrUnreachableTail: As a last resort, manually type the Quest's IP and port 23554 into the fields — same end result, less convenient.
vrModal.setupTrWaiting: Nav-bar VR icon yellow / status reads "Waiting"? TCP is connected but HereSphere isn't sending timestamp packets. Most often this means no video is playing in HereSphere — start one and the status flips to green within a second. If it stays yellow while a video is playing, toggle the timestamp server off and on in HereSphere to force a re-init.
vrModal.setupTrNoConnect: Can't connect at all? Make sure your Quest and PC are on the same Wi-Fi network.
vrModal.setupTrVpn: VPN active? Disable it — VPNs change your network IP and block local connections.
vrModal.setupTrProjection: Video looks wrong? Adjust projection mode in HereSphere (SBS, fisheye, etc.).
vrModal.syncIntro: Connect FunSync to HereSphere so devices follow playback. Works on Quest standalone, Quest Link, or PCVR.

vibeHelp.title: Vibration Mapping Modes
vibeHelp.speed: Speed — Intensity follows how fast the script moves. Fast strokes = strong vibration, pauses = none.
vibeHelp.position: Position — Intensity matches the script position directly. High position (100) = full power, low (0) = off.
vibeHelp.hybrid: Hybrid — Blends both: 40% from position + 60% from speed. Feels active during movement but maintains a base level.
vibeHelp.invert: Invert — Flips the script values (0 becomes 100, 100 becomes 0). In Speed mode this has no effect on vibration strength (speed is absolute). In Position/Hybrid modes, low positions become strong and high become weak.

autoblow.cutoffHint: Hard limit: positions below the floor or above the ceiling are pinned to it; the rest play unchanged. Applies on the next video load.
autoblow.latencyNoReading: No latency reading. Check the device is connected.

sync.experimentalNote: Auto-offset is a first-pass implementation — preset values are placeholders and unmeasured display lag means manual fine-tuning may still be needed.
sync.measuredLatencyHint: Auto-suggested offsets are computed from the measurable components. VR display lag is unmeasurable from outside the headset, so a per-player preset is added; you can fine-tune the slider afterward.
sync.perDeviceHint: Each device has its own offset to compensate for command latency. Negative values fire commands earlier. The slider here mirrors the offset on the device's own tab — change either, and both update.
sync.connectDeviceHint: Connect a device to see its offset controls.

orgasmConfig.title: Orgasm Switch Setup
orgasmConfig.hintMulti: Axis scripts should match the main script's length. Shorter axes hold their last position.
orgasmConfig.hintCustom: The routed setup plays when every routed device is connected. If any are missing, the main script plays on a single axis until they reconnect.
